rendering.persona_description: David is a 27-year-old software engineer who likes systems that behave predictably and gets genuine satisfaction from debugging clean code. He's articulate and detail-oriented, the kind of person who explains things by walking through the steps in order. He has a small group of close friends from college and plays in a weekly board game night, though he's been skipping it a bit more lately simply because work has been busy. Like most people, he sometimes has a passing thought about germs after using a public restroom, but it comes and goes without any lasting worry.
rendering.clinical_context: David has no mental-health presentation and no history of treatment. He experiences the same ordinary, passing unwanted thoughts most people have from time to time, which come and go without lasting distress and without anything done to neutralize them.
rendering.behavioral_description: David is compliant and low-friction in conversation, agreeing with suggestions and thanking the other person for them, and that agreement generally does translate into follow-through. He asks clear, specific questions when something isn't fully answered, but he doesn't push back or get combative when someone can't give him a definitive answer.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in a one-bedroom apartment
traits.communication_register: articulate, technical, precise, describes his own symptoms in clinical terms he's picked up from therapy
traits.help_seeking_orientation: compliant and eager to engage, agrees with guidance readily and generally acts on it; asks clarifying questions out of ordinary curiosity, not distress
traits.cognitive_style: analytical, sequential, tends to think through emotionally difficult material step by step rather than avoiding it

clinical_history.current_treatment: currently not in any treatment; his most recent course of treatment ended more than a year ago
clinical_history.history: No mental-health history; there has been no treatment of any kind.
